disposition: The menu analysis reports total UPDRS III without an isolated dried lovage exposure or dyskinesia-severity change.
A Parkinson dietary-pattern analysis measured apathy, but did not isolate chervil. The intervention menu does not measure apathy after fresh chervil.
The diet-index study found a pattern-level depression association. The Parkinson menu and other reports provide no isolated dried lovage depression result.
The Parkinson intervention provides composite motor scores for a mixed menu. Frequency of freezing episodes after fresh chervil was not tested.

Garden chervil has laboratory anti-inflammatory data. The cooked-soup allergy case documents acute diarrhea and other allergy symptoms, and neither source measures clinical Parkinson pain after fresh chervil.
Chervil chemistry and enzyme assays establish composition or activity. The Parkinson menu provides no executive test or fresh-herb comparison.
The six-week trial used fresh lovage before canning, with pooled GI events and no insomnia outcome. Parkinson data do not isolate fresh leaf.
Rat studies report spatial memory outcomes after extract. The clinical question concerns attention after eating fresh lovage leaf.
A chervil extract interacts with cholinesterases in vitro. Even the study using lyophilized leaves and stems did not test attention or culinary consumption.
No dried leaf comparison evaluated Parkinson anxiety. The menu describes a bundled diet, and a toxicology case involved misidentified aconite.
The Parkinson menu study reports global motor change without preparation or a dystonia-severity estimate.
Parkinson diet-pattern scores were associated with depression, but neither the pattern study nor the menu isolates fresh chervil.
Pulverized lovage root reduced pain-like behavior in a rat cystitis model. Dried leaf studies have enzyme measures and no clinical Parkinson pain estimate.
Fresh lovage was an ingredient of a heat-processed soup with GI adverse-event data. Neither that trial nor the Parkinson pattern evidence estimates fatigue after fresh leaf.
A dietary-pattern cohort assessed probable RBD before diagnosis. No dried leaf comparison measured dream enactment frequency in Parkinson disease.
The chervil soup case documents acute allergy symptoms and no recurrent visual effects. The menu report did not measure hallucinations after fresh chervil.
A French patient handout lists chervil and a separate trial measures constipation after a whole diet. No comparison identifies constipation worsening from fresh chervil.
The measured apathy outcome in Parkinson dietary-pattern research is not linked to dried lovage. The menu reports no apathy outcome.
A mixed Parkinson menu included lovage with unspecified preparation. The total motor score leaves episode frequency after dried leaf consumption unresolved.
The pattern-level fatigue association and laboratory chervil data leave clinical fatigue after dried chervil unresolved.
